newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus plans five-year government bonds.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus plans five-year government bonds.

text.p: Cyprus's central bank plans to auction five-year government bonds and to introduce secondary trading of the issues on the island's stock market, a bank official said on Wednesday.
"We hope to launch them in the first six months of next year," George Thoma, manager of the central bank's domestic banking operation department, told Reuters.
"The stock will have a nominal interest rate. The yield will be established through auction procedures," he said.
The Central Bank hopes the new bonds will attract institutional investors such as banks, insurance companies and pension funds, although they will also be available to individuals.
"The policy with respect to foreign investors is still being examined," said Thoma.
The Central Bank will have the right of intervention on the secondary market to ensure the smooth operation of the system.
Creation of a secondary market for bonds is the third step taken by the Central Bank since January this year for the creation of a money market to act as a tool of monetary policy.
It auctions 91-day treasury bills twice a month to fund government financing requirements and holds repos and reverse repos of treasury bills when required to manage commercial banks' liquidity.
The Central Bank currently sells three-year government development bonds to the public. There is no secondary trading in those bonds.
